title: Minimum Absolute Difference in BST
question: Why compare only adjacent inorder values?
answer: Inorder traversal of a BST is sorted, and the minimum difference in a sorted sequence occurs between adjacent elements.

title: Minimum Absolute Difference in BST
question: What is the central idea behind Minimum Absolute Difference in BST?
answer: Inorder traversal yields sorted values, so only adjacent values need comparison.

title: K-diff Pairs in an Array
question: Why must k=0 be handled separately?
answer: A zero difference requires two occurrences of the same value, while positive k pairs can be counted by checking whether x+k exists among distinct values.

title: K-diff Pairs in an Array
question: What is the central idea behind K-diff Pairs in an Array?
answer: Use a set of distinct values and count each value whose value+k exists; when k is zero, count values appearing at least twice.

title: Encode and Decode TinyURL
question: What invariant must encode/decode preserve?
answer: Every issued short key maps to exactly its original URL, so decoding an encoded URL returns the original input.

title: Encode and Decode TinyURL
question: What is the central idea behind Encode and Decode TinyURL?
answer: Assign each new URL a unique incrementing key and store forward and reverse mappings; this is an in-memory design suitable for the judge.

title: Complex Number Multiplication
question: Why is the real part ac-bd?
answer: Because i²=-1, the product bd·i² contributes -bd to the real component.

title: Complex Number Multiplication
question: What is the central idea behind Complex Number Multiplication?
answer: Parse real and imaginary components and apply (a+bi)(c+di)=(ac-bd)+(ad+bc)i.

title: Convert BST to Greater Tree
question: Why use reverse inorder rather than ordinary inorder?
answer: Reverse inorder visits larger values first, allowing a running sum of all greater-or-equal original values to be accumulated before updating each node.

title: Convert BST to Greater Tree
question: What is the central idea behind Convert BST to Greater Tree?
answer: Reverse inorder visits nodes in descending order; maintain a running sum and replace each node's value with that sum.

title: Minimum Time Difference
question: Why compare the last time with the first time plus 24 hours?
answer: Time wraps at midnight, so the circular gap between the latest and earliest times may be the smallest difference.

title: Minimum Time Difference
question: What is the central idea behind Minimum Time Difference?
answer: Convert times to minutes after midnight, sort them, compare neighbors and also compare the wraparound gap across midnight.

title: Single Element in a Sorted Array
question: Why force the midpoint to an even index?
answer: Before the singleton, each pair begins at an even index; comparing an even midpoint with its next element identifies whether the singleton lies to the right or at/before that pair.

title: Single Element in a Sorted Array
question: What is the central idea behind Single Element in a Sorted Array?
answer: Use binary search and align the midpoint to an even index; pair structure tells which half contains the singleton.

title: Reverse String II
question: Why advance by 2k after each reversal?
answer: The rule affects only the first k characters of each 2k block; the next block begins exactly 2k positions later.

title: Reverse String II
question: What is the central idea behind Reverse String II?
answer: Convert to a mutable character array and reverse the range beginning at each 2k block.

title: 01 Matrix
question: Why initialize the queue with every zero?
answer: All zero cells are distance-zero sources, so multi-source BFS expands by increasing distance and computes nearest-zero distances in linear time.

title: 01 Matrix
question: What is the central idea behind 01 Matrix?
answer: Start BFS simultaneously from all zero cells; expanding outward assigns each cell its shortest distance to a zero.

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
question: Why is the diameter through a node leftHeight + rightHeight?
answer: The longest path that passes through a node descends through its left subtree and right subtree, so its edge count is the sum of those subtree heights.

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
question: What is the central idea behind Diameter of Binary Tree?
answer: For each node, combine left and right subtree heights to update the best diameter; return the node's height to its parent.
